analysis.title: Investment Strategy Weekly (November 13, 2026): Regulatory Fears Regarding the AI Buildout Are Likely Overblown
key_insights: Tech has lagged the S&P 500 by 9.3% quarter-to-date after outperforming by 1,608 bps through September. It is on pace for its worst quarterly relative performance since 3Q02. Cited drivers are AI capex concerns, increased equity issuance and midterm policy implications. Raymond James calls the cooling seasonal rather than fundamental and gives five reasons to stay optimistic on Technology.

Equity supply overhang: Anthropic is set to go public Thursday Nov 19 in what could be the second-largest IPO ever, behind SpaceX. It is reportedly targeting a market cap above $1.5T and is well oversubscribed. The S-1 shows robust revenue growth, expanding compute commitments and declining compute costs as a share of revenue. The firm says this may ease concerns over AI funding and demand durability.

State-level data center moratoriums mainly affect future pipeline projects, not those under construction. Power capacity under construction is more than 1.5x that of existing facilities. Duke Energy, Micron, GE Vernova and Seagate commentary points to strong demand and backlogs through at least 2028.

Tech has fallen ~10% during 3Q26 earnings season, its worst earnings-season performance since 1Q22. The prior 10 earnings seasons averaged a 4.5% gain. Consensus 2027 EPS estimates for Tech have risen 3.4% since the season began, the second-largest upward revision of any sector after Energy. The firm calls the selloff disconnected from fundamentals.

Consensus expects 2027 Tech EPS growth to outpace the rest of the index by 37%, versus a 34% premium this year. Semiconductors are projected to drive ~60% of next year's EPS growth. Leading chipmakers signal demand exceeding supply through at least 2027, supporting expectations of 67% semiconductor EPS growth next year.

Tech sector aggregate free cash flow is projected to grow 52% in 2026 and 46% in 2027, versus 5% and -6% for the S&P 500 ex Tech. Select hyperscalers have seen FCF declines from funding AI infrastructure.
Hyperscaler cloud revenue grew 63% YoY in 3Q26, accelerating from 54% in 2Q26. Cloud backlogs rose 141% to $1.8T. Per Ramp, 57% of businesses now use AI-related products, up from 44% a year ago.

Tech NTM P/E has fallen 32% despite a 15% YTD gain, the steepest contraction at this point in a year since 2008. It started 2026 at 27x, near its highest since 2002. The sector is at its lowest multiple since 2020 and at a discount to the S&P 500 for the first time since 2019. The firm says much of the bad news is priced in.

October headline CPI rose 0.4% MoM and core 0.3%, both hotter than expected. The firm estimates annual inflation at +4.0% headline and +2.8% core and reinforces its view of a 25bp rate hike in December.
October headline PPI rose 0.3% MoM, slightly below expectations, with the yearly rate at +6.5%, the fastest since November 2022. Food and core goods prices drove the monthly rise.
Existing home sales fell 5.5% MoM in October to 3.75m, the lowest since August 2010. Inventory rose to 5.1 months supply and median home price growth slowed to 0.4% YoY.

Consumer Discretionary is up 6% month-to-date, which would be its largest monthly outperformance versus the S&P 500 since November 2024 if it holds. Its LTM valuation is near the lowest since 2018 and consensus 2027 EPS growth of -4% is the third lowest of any sector. The firm stays overweight and calls it a contrarian trade, expecting further moderation in rates and oil.

Treasury yields surged on hot core CPI and hawkish Fed commentary. The 2-year rose 35 bps week-to-date, its biggest weekly rise since October 2024. The 10-year rose 28 bps, its largest since April 2025, and is back above 5%. A December hike is fully priced with ~72% odds of another in January, and the 2s10s curve is near its flattest since March 2025.

The five largest hyperscalers have issued ~$300B of bonds this year. Foreign currency deals total ~$92.5B, more than the group's entire USD issuance in 2025. Alphabet raised the equivalent of $46.25B across eight foreign currencies versus $45B in dollar bonds.
S&P 500 is up 0.3% in the nine days since the midterm elections, versus a historical average of 0.6% since 1930.

US retail gasoline is below $4.00/gal for the first time since the US-Iran conflict resumed in July. The firm sees gasoline averaging about $3.50 in 2027 if a durable US-Iran deal is reached by next spring. Per-capita gasoline consumption is tracking to a post-COVID low of 390 gallons, versus 440 a decade ago.

sector_views.rationale: Earnings, FCF growth and cloud backlogs are strong, valuation has reset to a discount to the S&P 500, and the firm calls the selloff disconnected from fundamentals.
The firm calls it a contrarian trade: valuation is near the lowest since 2018 and sentiment is subdued, while moderating rates and oil should support consumer spending.
